newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. June T-bonds rise above 108-30/32.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. June T-bonds rise above 108-30/32.

text.p: U.S. June T-bond futures rose above 108-30/32, as selling from hedge funds dried up after several days of long liquidation, technical traders and analysts said.
"Once people realized there was no follow-through hedge fund selling, they started to bid the market back up," one bond market analyst said.

Total open interest in bond futures was up slightly on Tuesday after shrinking more than 94,000 contracts from its all-time high of 602,440 on May 13. Some analysts attributed the decline to long liquidation from hedge funds.

The record high open interest was set on the same day that June T-bonds rose to a 2-1/2-month high at 110-22/32, and indicated to some analysts that there were no more participants willing to establish long positions at that high.
The selling pressure was not as strong on Tuesday as some traders had expected, and total bond futures open interest rose about 500 contracts.
In addition, some technical analysts said short-term market conditions in T-bonds had become oversold.
"I'm a little bullish here, yes, but not excruciatingly so," Kalivas said, adding that he was even less bullish for Eurodollars. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))

"The hourly chart has accrued a fairly significant oversold condition and the market is on the verge of moving into a fairly solid zone of support," Stewart Taylor, an analyst, said before the opening in his Taylor Fixed-Income Outlook newsletter.
Some analysts said a failure to close above 108-30/32 would point to further declines later in the week.

Nick Kalivas, senior credit market analyst at Refco Inc, said there was a buy-the-dip mentality and that there was low risk to the upside in June bond futures. September bonds become lead contract month in Thursday's evening session.
